cmo-cmo-1993-01.prompt: Determine a triangle for which the three sides and an altitude are four consecutive integers and for which this altitude partitions the triangle into two right triangles with integer sides. Show that there is only one such triangle.
cmo-cmo-1993-01.answer: The $13$–$14$–$15$ triangle with altitude $12$ onto the side $14$, which splits it into the $5$–$12$–$13$ and $9$–$12$–$15$ right triangles.

cmo-cmo-1993-02.prompt:
Show that the number $x$ is rational if and only if three distinct terms that form a geometric progression can be chosen from the sequence
$$x,\ x+1,\ x+2,\ x+3,\ \ldots$$
cmo-cmo-1993-02.answer: From $(x+b)^2 = (x+a)(x+c)$ with $a < b < c$ one gets $x(2b - a - c) = ac - b^2$ with $2b \ne a + c$; conversely for $x + a = \frac mq > 0$ take $\frac mq,\ \frac mq(q+1),\ \frac mq(q+1)^2$.

cmo-cmo-1993-03.prompt: In triangle $ABC$, the medians to the sides $AB$ and $AC$ are perpendicular. Prove that $\cot B + \cot C \ge \frac23$.
cmo-cmo-1993-03.answer: With the centroid $G$ at the origin, $B = (p, 0)$, $C = (0, q)$: $\cot B + \cot C = \frac{a^2}{2[ABC]} = \frac{p^2 + q^2}{3pq} \ge \frac23$ (equality iff $AB = AC$).

cmo-cmo-1993-04.prompt: A number of schools took part in a tennis tournament. No two players from the same school played against each other. Every two players from different schools played exactly one match against each other. A match between two boys or between two girls was called a *single* and that between a boy and a girl was called a *mixed single*. The total number of boys differed from the total number of girls by at most $1$. The total number of singles differed from the total number of mixed singles by at most $1$. At most how many schools were represented by an odd number of players?

cmo-cmo-1993-05.prompt:
Let $y_1, y_2, y_3, \ldots$ be a sequence such that $y_1 = 1$ and, for $k > 0$, is defined by the relationship:
$$y_{2k} = \begin{cases} 2y_k & \text{if } k \text{ is even} \\ 2y_k + 1 & \text{if } k \text{ is odd} \end{cases} \qquad y_{2k+1} = \begin{cases} 2y_k & \text{if } k \text{ is odd} \\ 2y_k + 1 & \text{if } k \text{ is even} \end{cases}$$
Show that the sequence $y_1, y_2, y_3, \ldots$ takes on every positive integer value exactly once.
cmo-cmo-1993-05.answer: $\{y_{2k}, y_{2k+1}\} = \{2y_k, 2y_k + 1\}$, so by induction $n \mapsto y_n$ permutes each block $[2^{m-1}, 2^m - 1]$. (In fact $y_n$ is the Gray code $n \oplus \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.)
